title: Psalm 70: Hurry, O LORD, to Help Me
summary: In five short verses a poor and needy person begs God to hurry to his rescue. He asks that those who seek his life be turned back in shame, and that all who seek God rejoice and say that God is great. The psalm ends where it began, with an urgent plea: do not delay.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 70
from.text: a compact example of the lament form

line: In five short verses a poor and needy person begs God to hurry to help him, and still stops to pray that all who seek God would rejoice.
guide: Some prayers have no time for long words; a plea for God to hurry is a full prayer, for a hospital corridor or a sleepless night. Notice that even this urgent prayer stops to think of others who seek God.

stanzas.title: Turn back those who seek my life
Let all who seek You rejoice
Poor and needy: do not delay

verses.t: For the choirmaster. Of David. To bring remembrance. Make haste, O God, to deliver me! Hurry, O LORD, to help me!
May those who seek my life be ashamed and confounded; may those who wish me harm be repelled and humiliated.
May those who say, “Aha, aha!” retreat because of their shame.
May all who seek You rejoice and be glad in You; may those who love Your salvation always say, “Let God be magnified!”
But I am poor and needy; hurry to me, O God. You are my help and my deliverer; O LORD, do not delay.
